readerTension.whatReaderIsConfusedAbout: How a face can feel oily and uncomfortable at the same time.
readerTension.whatReaderIsAnxiousAbout: Making shine worse by choosing the wrong texture or damaging their skin with too many changes.
readerTension.decisionReaderNeedsToMake: Whether to simplify, observe, use a scan, or seek professional input.

categoryManagerPov.whatToChoose: One small, comfort-first observation before changing a whole routine.
categoryManagerPov.whatToAvoid: Aggressively stripping oil, escalating multiple actives, or treating an online explanation as diagnosis.
categoryManagerPov.whereBuyersGoWrong: They frame oil and hydration as opposites and buy for one while ignoring the other.
categoryManagerPov.whatTheBrandBelieves: A better first decision comes from describing what is visible and felt, then respecting the limits of that description.
tradeoffsThatMatter: one adjustment versus a full routine reset

plannedExamples: A Bengaluru commuter is shiny around the T-zone after a humid commute but feels tight after cleansing; both observations belong in the picture.
A reader in an air-conditioned office keeps buying heavier creams because their cheeks feel uncomfortable, but wants a next step that does not assume their whole face is dry.

mistakesToCover: treating oil as proof that hydration is unnecessary
self-diagnosing irritation or pain from a cosmetic guide

conditions: a rapidly changing, painful, bleeding, or persistent skin concern
a reader seeking diagnosis or prescription treatment

brandPov.statement: MyMirror can organise what is visibly present today; it cannot identify the medical reason a concern is happening.

finalClosingBeforeCta.plannedClosing: You do not have to choose between fighting shine and feeling comfortable. Start by naming both, then make one calm next move.
